Enel Generacion Peru SAA Reports Steady Performance in Latest Results, Highlights Resilient Energy Demand

Lima—Enel Generacion Peru SAA, one of the country’s leading electric utilities, reported its most recent financial results on Thursday, posting stable earnings amid signs of resilient energy demand in Peru’s recovering economy.

The company reported revenues of PEN 1.02 billion for the quarter ended March 31, up 3.1% from the same period last year, driven by a modest increase in both industrial and residential electricity consumption. Net profit for the quarter reached PEN 168 million, compared to PEN 162 million in the first quarter of 2023, reflecting controlled operating costs and effective asset management.

CEO Javier Morales commented, “Our results this quarter reflect Enel Generacion Peru SAA’s commitment to operational excellence and reliable service. Despite a complex macroeconomic environment, we have continued to deliver for our customers and maintain solid financial health.”

Electricity demand in Peru has shown gradual improvement since the latter half of 2023, as manufacturing and mining activity picked up and urbanization trends continued. According to the Peruvian Association of Electric Utilities, total power consumption increased 2.7% year-on-year in the first quarter.

Analysts noted the company’s ability to manage costs despite inflationary pressures and currency volatility. “Enel Generacion Peru SAA has again demonstrated its resilience, maintaining profitability even as input costs rise,” said Luis Espinoza, senior utilities analyst at Andina Securities. “Their diversified generation portfolio—balancing hydroelectric and thermal assets—has proven advantageous given recent rainfall patterns.”

The company’s EBITDA stood at PEN 320 million, up 4% from a year ago, while capital expenditures for the period totaled PEN 54 million, with investments focused on maintenance and incremental upgrades to generation facilities. Morales indicated that Enel Generacion Peru SAA’s ongoing projects are on schedule, with no major delays or overruns.

Looking ahead, the company reaffirmed its full-year guidance, anticipating continued growth in energy sales and stable margins. “We remain committed to supporting Peru’s energy transition and to investing in reliable, sustainable infrastructure,” Morales said.

Enel Generacion Peru SAA shares closed up 0.8% on the Lima Stock Exchange following the announcement, outperforming the broader utilities sector index. Investors and analysts will be watching for further updates on the company’s capital spending plans and regulatory developments in the coming months, as the industry adapts to evolving demand trends and Peru’s economic outlook.
